candidates.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
candidates.summary: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. candidates.title: CAEL 0.4.1: a chat assistant with no neural network and no transformer
candidates.summary:
Hi all. I’d like to share CAEL, a hobby project: a chat assistant built without any neural network. No transformer, no neural weights, no LLM behind the replies. It runs on a CPU in plain Python.

How it works

  • Symbolic, count-based and cellular-automaton engines for reasoning and state.
  • Exact skills for conversation: quantities, rates, clock times, syllogisms, schedules and changed values.
  • Chat memory: it answers from what you said earlier in the conversation.
  • Checked web answers: when it doesn’t know, it searches and answers
